title: I'd like to book a meeting room
grammar: would like / I'd like (pedidos e ofertas educadas)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a fazer pedidos e oferecer ajuda com elegância usando would like e I'd like. Como assistente administrativo da Delta Ducon, você atende visitantes, marca compromissos e apoia a diretoria o tempo todo — e would like é a estrutura que deixa cada pedido educado e profissional.
intro: At reception, an assistant offers and requests things all day. Would you like a coffee? I'd like to book a meeting room for ten. These polite forms make every visitor feel welcome.
Today we practise would like and its short form I'd like. We use them for polite requests and kind offers, and they sound softer than want at the front desk of Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Good morning, welcome to Delta Ducon. Would you like a coffee or a glass of water? I would like to help you today. I'd like to book a meeting room for our visitor. Let us practise polite requests and offers together.
vocab: I would like to book an appointment for Friday.
Would you like to leave a message for the director?
The client would like a copy of the contract.
Would you like a visitor badge for the day?
The supplier would like a receipt for the payment.
Would you like a glass of water while you wait?
practice: I would like to book an ______ with the manager for Monday.
Would you like to leave a ______ for the director?
The visitor would like a ______ of the signed report.
Would you like a visitor ______ at reception?
The client would like a ______ for the payment, please.
Would you like a glass of ______ while you wait?
I would like a ______ of the ISO certificate for the file.
Would you like to make an ______ with the engineering team?

audio.title: Welcome to reception
audio.text: Good morning, and welcome to Delta Ducon. Would you like to sit down while I call the director? I'd like to offer you a coffee or a glass of water. Our visitor would like to book a meeting room for ten o'clock. He'd also like a copy of the last proposal. If you'd like to leave a message, I can write it down for you. We'd like to make your visit comfortable.

readAloud: I'd like to book a meeting room for ten.
Would you like a coffee while you wait?
The director would like a copy of the report.
Would you like to leave a message?
We'd like to confirm the appointment for Friday.
fill: I ___ to book a meeting room for Monday. (like)
Would you ___ a coffee or a tea? (like)
The director ___ a copy of the contract. (like)
Would the client ___ a receipt for the payment? (like)
We ___ to confirm the appointment for Friday. (like)
___ you like to leave a message? (would)
She ___ to speak to the manager, please. (like)
I ___ a glass of water, please. (like)
qa: Would you like a coffee?
Yes, please, I'd like a coffee.
What would you like to do first?
I'd like to book a meeting room.
Would the client like a copy of the report?
Yes, he'd like a copy, please.
Would you like to leave a message?
Yes, I'd like to leave a message for the director.
What time would you like the appointment?
I'd like the appointment at ten o'clock.

a.label: I'd like ...
a.placeholder: I'd like to book a meeting room.

sentences: I'd like to book a meeting room for ten.
Would you like a coffee or a glass of water?
The director would like a copy of the proposal.
Would you like to leave a message for the team?
We'd like to confirm the appointment for Friday.
The client would like a receipt for the payment.
Would you like a visitor badge at reception?
I'd like to speak to the engineering team, please.
grammarPoint: would like é a forma educada de want (querer). Usamos para pedidos e ofertas gentis. A forma curta é 'd like: I would like = I'd like. Depois de would like usamos to + verbo ou um substantivo. Para ofertas, pergunte Would you like ...?. I'd like to book a room. — Eu gostaria de reservar uma sala. Would you like a coffee? — Você gostaria de um café?
deepDive: Cuidado: would like nunca muda com he/she/it — não existe 'would likes'. Certo: She would like a copy. Depois de would like a coisa, use to + verbo (I'd like to confirm) ou direto o substantivo (I'd like a receipt). Na resposta educada, diga Yes, please ou No, thank you. A contração 'd serve para I'd, you'd, he'd, she'd, we'd, they'd.
examples: I'd like to book an appointment.
Eu gostaria de marcar um compromisso.
Would you like a glass of water?
Você gostaria de um copo de água?
The director would like a copy of the report.
O diretor gostaria de uma cópia do relatório.
We'd like to confirm the meeting.
Nós gostaríamos de confirmar a reunião.
Would you like to leave a message?
Você gostaria de deixar um recado?
She'd like to speak to the manager.
Ela gostaria de falar com o gerente.
I'd like a receipt for the payment, please.
Eu gostaria de um recibo do pagamento, por favor.
They'd like a visitor badge for the day.
Eles gostariam de um crachá de visitante para o dia.
mistakes: I would like book a room.
I would like to book a room.
Depois de would like usamos to + verbo.
She would likes a copy.
She would like a copy.
would like nunca leva -s com he/she/it.
Do you like a coffee?
Would you like a coffee?
Para uma oferta educada usamos Would you like.
I would like to a receipt.
I would like a receipt.
Antes de um substantivo não usamos to.
I like to book a room, please.
I'd like to book a room, please.
Para o pedido educado usamos would like, não like.
quick: She ___ a copy of the report. (like)
___ you like to leave a message? (would)

celebrate.en: Well done. Polite offers and requests are the heart of great reception work — and now you make them naturally in English.
celebrate.pt: Muito bem. Ofertas e pedidos educados são o coração de uma boa recepção — e agora você os faz com naturalidade em inglês.

title: What's happening next week?
grammar: Present Continuous para arranjos futuros (compromissos com data/hora)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a usar o Present Continuous (am/is/are + verbo-ing) para falar de compromissos já marcados no futuro. Como assistente administrativo da Delta Ducon, você organiza a agenda da diretoria e confirma visitas de fornecedores e auditores — e essa é a forma natural de dizer o que já está agendado.
intro: When a meeting is already in the diary, we use the Present Continuous for the future. The auditors are visiting on Monday. The director is flying to Uberlândia on Tuesday.
Today we practise the Present Continuous for fixed arrangements. It is the natural way to talk about appointments with a date and a time at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Let me check the diary with you. The supplier is coming to the plant on Thursday. The director is meeting the client on Friday at ten. I am confirming the flights this afternoon. Today we learn the Present Continuous for future arrangements. Let us begin.
vocab: The supplier is coming to the plant on Thursday.
The auditor is visiting us next Monday.
The team is attending a conference in June.
The delivery is arriving on Monday morning.
The director is taking a trip to Uberlândia.
I am checking the schedule for next week.
practice: The ______ is coming to the plant on Thursday.
The ISO ______ is visiting us next Monday.
The engineering team is attending a ______ in June.
The ______ of filter bags is arriving tomorrow morning.
The director is taking a ______ to Uberlândia next week.
I am updating the ______ for the whole team.
The ______ is sending the quote on Friday.
We are confirming the ______ date with the client.

audio.title: The diary for next week
audio.text: Next week is very busy at Delta Ducon. On Monday, the ISO auditor is visiting the Diadema plant at nine. On Tuesday, the director is flying to Uberlândia to meet a cement client. The supplier is delivering the filter bags on Wednesday morning. On Thursday, the engineering team is attending a conference on dust collection. I am booking the meeting rooms today, and I am confirming the flights this afternoon. Everything is arranged.

readAloud: The auditors are visiting us on Monday.
The director is flying to Uberlândia on Tuesday.
I am meeting the supplier on Friday at ten.
The delivery is arriving tomorrow morning.
We are attending a conference next month.
fill: The client ___ arriving at ten tomorrow. (be)
The auditors ___ visiting us next week. (be)
I ___ meeting the supplier on Friday. (be)
The director is ___ to Uberlândia on Tuesday. (fly)
We are ___ the training on Monday morning. (start)
The team is ___ for Diadema after lunch. (leave)
She is ___ the meeting room for ten o'clock. (book)
They ___ arriving on Thursday for the audit. (be)
qa: What are you doing on Monday?
I'm meeting the supplier at the plant.
When is the auditor visiting?
The auditor is visiting on Monday morning.
Is the director travelling next week?
Yes, he's flying to Uberlândia on Tuesday.
When is the delivery arriving?
The delivery is arriving tomorrow morning.
What is the team doing in June?
The team is attending a conference.

a.label: I'm ...-ing on ...
a.placeholder: I'm meeting the supplier on Friday.

b.label: is / are ...-ing
b.placeholder: The auditors are visiting on Monday.

sentences: The auditors are visiting us on Monday.
The director is flying to Uberlândia on Tuesday.
I'm meeting the supplier on Friday at ten.
The delivery is arriving tomorrow morning.
We are attending a conference in June.
The team is leaving for Diadema after lunch.
She is booking the meeting room for the client.
They are starting the training on Monday.
grammarPoint: Usamos o Present Continuous (am/is/are + verbo-ing) para compromissos já marcados no futuro, geralmente com data ou hora. Escolhemos am com I, is com he/she/it e are com you/we/they. The auditors are visiting on Monday. — Os auditores vêm na segunda-feira. I'm meeting the client at ten. — Eu vou encontrar o cliente às dez.
deepDive: A diferença entre o Present Simple e este uso: o Present Simple é para horários fixos e repetidos (The train leaves at nine), enquanto o Present Continuous futuro é para um plano combinado (I'm leaving at nine tomorrow). Sempre indique quando: on Monday, at ten, next week. Formação do -ing: make/making (tira o -e), get/getting (dobra a consoante).
examples: The supplier is coming on Thursday.
O fornecedor vem na quinta-feira.
I'm meeting the director at nine.
Eu vou me reunir com o diretor às nove.
The auditors are visiting next week.
Os auditores vêm na próxima semana.
We are attending a conference in June.
Nós vamos participar de uma conferência em junho.
The delivery is arriving tomorrow.
A entrega chega amanhã.
She is flying to Uberlândia on Tuesday.
Ela viaja de avião para Uberlândia na terça-feira.
They are starting the training on Monday.
Eles começam o treinamento na segunda-feira.
I'm booking the meeting room this afternoon.
Eu vou reservar a sala de reunião esta tarde.
mistakes: The auditors is visiting on Monday.
The auditors are visiting on Monday.
Com um sujeito no plural usamos are.
I meeting the supplier tomorrow.
I'm meeting the supplier tomorrow.
Falta o verbo be: I am / I'm.
He is fly to Uberlândia on Tuesday.
He is flying to Uberlândia on Tuesday.
Depois de be o verbo leva -ing.
The director is meet the client on Friday.
The director is meeting the client on Friday.
Falta o -ing no verbo principal.
We are attend a conference in June.
We are attending a conference in June.
O verbo principal precisa do -ing.
quick: He is ___ to Uberlândia on Tuesday. (fly)
We are ___ the training on Monday. (start)

celebrate.en: Excellent. You can now talk about a whole week of arrangements — a key skill for anyone who runs a busy diary.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Agora você consegue falar de toda uma semana de compromissos — uma habilidade essencial para quem cuida de uma agenda cheia.

title: Could you tell me where the meeting is?
grammar: Perguntas indiretas (Could you tell me where / when …?)
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender a fazer perguntas indiretas, mais educadas, com Could you tell me where / when / what …?. Como assistente administrativo da Delta Ducon, você orienta visitantes, atende o telefone e pede informações a colegas — e a pergunta indireta soa gentil e profissional.
intro: A direct question can sound abrupt. Where is the meeting? sounds better as Could you tell me where the meeting is? At reception, this softer form is very useful.
Today we practise indirect questions. The key is the word order: after Could you tell me where, we keep the normal order of a statement, without inverting the verb.
introAudio: Welcome. Could you tell me where you are going today? Could you tell me what time your meeting starts? Do you know where the reception is? Today we learn indirect questions, the polite way to ask for information. Let us practise together.
vocab: Could you tell me where the reception is?
Could you tell me where the visitor parking is?
Could you tell me what the director's extension is?
Could you tell me where the main entrance is?
Could you tell me where the restroom is?
Could you tell me which floor the meeting is on?
practice: Could you tell me where the ______ is, please?
Could you tell me where the visitor ______ is?
Do you know what the director's ______ number is?
Could you tell me where the main ______ is?
Could you tell me where the ______ is, please?
Could you tell me which ______ the meeting is on?
Do you know where the staff ______ is?
Could you tell me what the reception ______ is?

audio.title: Helping a visitor
audio.text: A visitor arrives at Delta Ducon and comes to the front desk. Could you tell me where the meeting room is, please? he asks. I explain that it is on the second floor. Then he asks: Do you know when the director is free? I check the diary and tell him. Could you tell me where the restroom is? he adds. I show him the way. Indirect questions make every conversation at reception calm and polite.

readAloud: Could you tell me where the reception is?
Could you tell me when the auditors arrive?
Do you know where the director is?
Could you tell me what time the meeting starts?
Do you know which floor the office is on?
fill: Could you tell me where the meeting ___? (be)
Could you tell me when the auditors ___? (arrive)
Do you know where the director ___? (be)
Could you tell me what time the training ___? (start)
Could you tell me how much the part ___? (cost)
Do you know where I ___ sign the form? (can)
Could you tell me who ___ the report? (send)
Could you tell me where the files ___? (be)
qa: Could you tell me where the meeting is?
Yes, it's on the second floor.
Could you tell me when the auditor arrives?
The auditor arrives at nine on Monday.
Do you know where the director is?
Yes, he's in the meeting room.
Could you tell me what the extension is?
The extension is two-four-one.
Do you know where the parking is?
Yes, the parking is behind the building.

a.label: Could you tell me where ...?
a.placeholder: Could you tell me where the reception is?

b.label: Do you know when ...?
b.placeholder: Do you know when the auditors arrive?

sentences: Could you tell me where the reception is?
Could you tell me when the meeting starts?
Do you know where the director is?
Could you tell me what the extension number is?
Do you know which floor the office is on?
Could you tell me how much the part costs?
Do you know where I can sign the form?
Could you tell me when the auditors arrive?
grammarPoint: A pergunta indireta começa com Could you tell me ... ou Do you know ... e é mais educada. O segredo é a ordem: depois de where/when/what, mantemos a ordem de uma frase afirmativa, sem inverter e sem do/does. Direto: Where is the meeting? Indireto: Could you tell me where the meeting is? — Você poderia me dizer onde é a reunião?
deepDive: Na pergunta direta invertemos o verbo (Where is the meeting?), mas na indireta NÃO (Could you tell me where the meeting is?). Também tiramos o do/does: direto What time does it start? / indireto Could you tell me what time it starts? Para perguntas de sim/não, use if ou whether: Do you know if the room is free?
examples: Could you tell me where the meeting is?
Você poderia me dizer onde é a reunião?
Do you know when the auditors arrive?
Você sabe quando os auditores chegam?
Could you tell me what the extension is?
Você poderia me dizer qual é o ramal?
Do you know where the director is?
Você sabe onde o diretor está?
Could you tell me what time it starts?
Você poderia me dizer a que horas começa?
Do you know if the room is free?
Você sabe se a sala está livre?
Could you tell me which floor it is on?
Você poderia me dizer em qual andar fica?
Do you know how much the part costs?
Você sabe quanto custa a peça?
mistakes: Could you tell me where is the meeting?
Could you tell me where the meeting is?
Na pergunta indireta não invertemos: the meeting is.
Could you tell me when do the auditors arrive?
Could you tell me when the auditors arrive?
Na indireta não usamos do/does.
Do you know where is the director?
Do you know where the director is?
Depois de where mantemos a ordem afirmativa.
Could you tell me what time does it start?
Could you tell me what time it starts?
Tiramos o does e conjugamos o verbo: it starts.
Do you know is the room free?
Do you know if the room is free?
Em pergunta de sim/não usamos if.
quick: Could you tell me where the meeting ___? (be)
Do you know when the auditors ___? (arrive)
Could you tell me what time it ___? (start)
Do you know where the director ___? (be)
Could you tell me where the files ___? (be)

celebrate.en: Great work. Indirect questions make you sound polished and professional at any front desk in the world.
celebrate.pt: Ótimo trabalho. As perguntas indiretas deixam você mais educado e profissional em qualquer recepção do mundo.

title: The meeting is at ten, isn't it?
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender as question tags (…isn't it? …don't they?) para confirmar informações com naturalidade. Como assistente administrativo da Delta Ducon, você confirma horários, prazos e detalhes de reuniões o dia inteiro — e a question tag é a forma amigável de checar se está tudo certo.
intro: We often check a fact instead of asking a full question. The meeting is at ten, isn't it? You sent the invoice, didn't you? The little tag at the end asks for confirmation.
Today we practise question tags. A positive sentence takes a negative tag, and a negative sentence takes a positive one. They make you sound friendly and sure when you confirm details at Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Let me confirm a few things with you. The meeting is at ten, isn't it? You have the ISO report, don't you? The auditors are coming on Monday, aren't they? Today we learn question tags, the natural way to check a fact. Let us practise together.
vocab: The deadline is Friday, isn't it?
The meeting starts at ten, doesn't it?
You sent the invoice, didn't you?
The supplier delivers on time, doesn't it?
You have the report ready, don't you?
The contract needs a signature, doesn't it?
practice: The ______ starts at ten o'clock, doesn't it?
You sent the ______ to finance, didn't you?
The ______ delivers the filter bags on time, doesn't it?
You have the ISO ______ ready, don't you?
The contract needs the director's ______, doesn't it?
You booked the ______ room for ten, didn't you?
We send the ______ every month, don't we?

audio.title: Confirming the details
audio.text: Before the visit, I like to confirm everything at Delta Ducon. The meeting is at ten, isn't it? Yes, the director says. You booked the room, didn't you? Of course. The auditors are coming on Monday, aren't they? Yes, they are. You sent the invoice to finance, didn't you? I check my email and confirm. The report is on your desk, isn't it? Question tags help me check every detail quickly and politely.

readAloud: The meeting is at ten, isn't it?
You have the report, don't you?
The auditors are coming on Monday, aren't they?
She works at reception, doesn't she?
You sent the invoice, didn't you?
fill: The meeting is at ten, ___ it? (isn't)
The auditors visit on Monday, ___ they? (don't)
The office opens at eight, ___ it? (doesn't)
qa: The meeting is at ten, isn't it?
Yes, it is, at ten sharp.
You sent the invoice, didn't you?
Yes, I did, this morning.
The auditors are coming on Monday, aren't they?
Yes, they are, at nine.
She works at reception, doesn't she?
Yes, she does, every day.
The deadline is Friday, isn't it?
Yes, it is, end of the day.

a.label: ..., isn't it?
a.placeholder: The meeting is at ten, isn't it?

b.label: ..., don't you?
b.placeholder: You have the report, don't you?

sentences: The meeting is at ten, isn't it?
You have the ISO report, don't you?
The auditors are coming on Monday, aren't they?
She works at reception, doesn't she?
You sent the invoice, didn't you?
The deadline is Friday, isn't it?
They deliver the filter bags on time, don't they?
The office opens at eight, doesn't it?
grammarPoint: A question tag é uma mini-pergunta no fim da frase para confirmar algo. A regra principal: frase afirmativa pede tag negativa, e frase negativa pede tag positiva. Usamos o mesmo auxiliar da frase (is/are/do/does/did). The meeting is at ten, isn't it? — A reunião é às dez, não é? You sent the invoice, didn't you? — Você enviou a fatura, não enviou?
deepDive: Escolha o auxiliar pelo verbo da frase: com be use is/are (The room is ready, isn't it?); com Present Simple use do/does (You work here, don't you?); no passado use did (You called, didn't you?). O pronome da tag repete o sujeito: it, they, you, she. Cuidado com I am → a tag é aren't I? (I'm on time, aren't I?).
examples: The meeting is at ten, isn't it?
A reunião é às dez, não é?
You have the report, don't you?
Você tem o relatório, não tem?
The auditors are coming, aren't they?
Os auditores estão vindo, não estão?
She works here, doesn't she?
Ela trabalha aqui, não trabalha?
You sent the invoice, didn't you?
Você enviou a fatura, não enviou?
The deadline is Friday, isn't it?
O prazo é sexta-feira, não é?
They deliver on time, don't they?
Eles entregam no prazo, não entregam?
The office opens at eight, doesn't it?
O escritório abre às oito, não abre?
mistakes: The meeting is at ten, isn't they?
The meeting is at ten, isn't it?
O pronome da tag deve combinar: the meeting → it.
You have the report, do you?
You have the report, don't you?
Frase afirmativa pede tag negativa.
She works here, doesn't it?
She works here, doesn't she?
O pronome deve ser she, não it.
The auditors are coming, isn't they?
The auditors are coming, aren't they?
Com sujeito plural usamos aren't they.
You sent the invoice, don't you?
You sent the invoice, didn't you?
A frase está no passado, então a tag usa didn't.
quick: The meeting is at ten, ___ it? (isn't)

celebrate.en: Very good. Question tags let you confirm details fast and sound like a natural English speaker at work.
celebrate.pt: Muito bom. As question tags permitem confirmar detalhes rapidamente e soar como um falante natural de inglês no trabalho.

title: I organise the files myself
objective: Nesta aula você vai aprender os pronomes reflexivos myself, yourself, himself, itself, ourselves e themselves. Como assistente administrativo da Delta Ducon, você faz muitas tarefas por conta própria e recebe visitantes com gentileza — e esses pronomes deixam claro quem realiza a ação e tornam o atendimento mais cordial.
intro: Sometimes the same person does and receives the action. I organise the files myself. Please help yourself to a coffee. The reflexive pronoun points back to the subject.
Today we practise reflexive pronouns. They show that you do something on your own, and they appear in polite phrases we use every day at reception in Delta Ducon.
introAudio: Welcome. Please help yourself to a coffee while you wait. I prepare the agenda myself every morning. The filter system cleans itself automatically. Today we learn reflexive pronouns like myself, yourself and themselves. Let us practise together.
vocab: Please help yourself to some water.
The director signs the contract himself.
The engineers do the checks themselves.
practice: I prepare the agenda ______ every morning.
Please help ______ to some coffee while you wait.
The engineers do the site checks ______.

audio.title: We do it ourselves
audio.text: At Delta Ducon, we like to be independent. I answer the phone and file the documents myself. The director often signs the contracts himself, without waiting for anyone. The baghouse cleans itself with an automatic pulse of air. When visitors arrive, I say: please help yourself to a coffee. The engineers manage the site checks themselves, and we prepare the audit files ourselves. A good team can do a lot by itself.

readAloud: I organise the files myself.
Please help yourself to a coffee.
The director signs the contract himself.
The system cleans itself automatically.
The engineers do the checks themselves.
fill: The machine stops ___ when it is full. (it)
qa: Who prepares the agenda?
I prepare it myself every morning.
Would you like a coffee?
Yes, thank you, I'll help myself.
Does the director sign the contracts?
Yes, he signs them himself.
How does the baghouse clean the bags?
It cleans itself automatically.
Who did the site checks?
The engineers did them themselves.

b.label: yourself / themselves
b.placeholder: Please help yourself to a coffee.

sentences: I organise the files myself.
Please help yourself to some coffee.
The director signs the contract himself.
The baghouse cleans itself automatically.
We prepare the audit files ourselves.
The engineers do the site checks themselves.
She books the meeting room herself.
Let me introduce myself to the visitor.
grammarPoint: Os pronomes reflexivos mostram que o sujeito faz e recebe a ação: myself (eu mesmo), yourself (você mesmo), himself (ele mesmo), herself (ela mesma), itself (ele/ela mesmo, para coisas), ourselves (nós mesmos), themselves (eles mesmos). I prepare the agenda myself. — Eu preparo a agenda eu mesmo. The system cleans itself. — O sistema se limpa sozinho.
deepDive: Repare no plural: -self vira -selves (myself → ourselves, yourself → yourselves, themselves). A expressão help yourself to ... significa 'sirva-se de ...'. Também usamos by + reflexivo para 'sozinho': I did it by myself. Cuidado: com ações do dia a dia que já são reflexivas em português, o inglês muitas vezes não usa o pronome (I get up, e não I get up myself).
examples: I organise the files myself.
Eu organizo os arquivos eu mesmo.
Please help yourself to a coffee.
Por favor, sirva-se de um café.
The director signs it himself.
O diretor assina ele mesmo.
The system cleans itself automatically.
O sistema se limpa automaticamente.
We prepared the report ourselves.
Nós preparamos o relatório nós mesmos.
The engineers do the checks themselves.
Os engenheiros fazem as verificações eles mesmos.
She books the room herself.
Ela reserva a sala ela mesma.
Let me introduce myself.
Deixe-me me apresentar.
mistakes: I prepare the agenda myselves.
I prepare the agenda myself.
Para uma pessoa é myself; myselves não existe.
Please help you to a coffee.
Please help yourself to a coffee.
A expressão correta é help yourself.
The director signs it hisself.
The director signs it himself.
A forma certa é himself, não hisself.
The engineers do it themself.
The engineers do it themselves.
No plural usamos themselves.
We prepared the report ourself.
We prepared the report ourselves.
Com we usamos ourselves, no plural.

celebrate.en: Outstanding. You've finished Module 2 — you can make polite requests, confirm details and describe your work with real confidence in English.
celebrate.pt: Excelente. Você concluiu o Módulo 2 — agora consegue fazer pedidos educados, confirmar detalhes e descrever seu trabalho com verdadeira confiança em inglês.
